system: You are a security investigator reviewing an alert. Base every claim only on the evidence available to you. Cite the record IDs that support each observation.

supporting_observations.claim: At 13:45:59 UTC, WS-MLOPEZ-01 sent 51,000,324 bytes to the explicit proxy over a 23.3-second HTTP connection; the proxy-side response was 9,053 bytes.
The available flow record identifies the proxy as the immediate destination, but does not identify the ultimate external destination, request URL, or transferred content.
At 13:30:20 UTC, PROXY-HD-01 initiated a TCP connection to WS-MLOPEZ-01 on port 9997; the flow transferred 40,513 bytes from the workstation to the proxy.
Cisco AnyConnect's VPN UI was launched on WS-MLOPEZ-01 at 13:23:45. The launch is not evidence that a VPN connection was established.
The large client-to-proxy transfer and the separate connection to port 9997 warrant investigation, but the available records do not establish that either was malicious.

known_telemetry_limitations: The provided evidence has a Zeek flow record for the large transfer but no corresponding proxy request record showing the URL, method, user, or upstream destination.
The supplied records do not identify which process generated the 13:45:59 transfer.
The port 9997 flow does not identify the workstation process listening on that port or the purpose of the connection.
claims_not_established: That the 51 MB flow reached an external destination rather than representing traffic only between the workstation and proxy.
That the transfer contained sensitive or otherwise unauthorized data.
That the transfer was initiated by AnyConnect or by any other specific application.
That AnyConnect established a VPN connection.
That the connection to port 9997 was a remote-control session or was related to the large transfer.
additional_evidence_needed: Retrieve PROXY-HD-01 access and TLS-inspection logs for the flow beginning at 13:45:59 UTC, including the upstream destination, request method, authenticated user, and byte counts.
Correlate endpoint process, socket, and file-access telemetry on WS-MLOPEZ-01 around 13:45:36–13:46:30 UTC to identify the process and any files involved.
Investigate the 13:30 connection to port 9997 using endpoint listener/process data and PROXY-HD-01 service and connection logs.
Check AnyConnect connection and client logs to determine whether it connected to a VPN endpoint.
If recoverable, examine browser, application, and file-transfer artifacts from WS-MLOPEZ-01 for evidence of the transfer's source and content.
